ledger_id_note: assigned by the coordinator (WP68 is lane 3's refinement_levels10_v1)
question: Confirmation of WP67 (STUDIES/trapped_chain_restart_v1): with the detector and restart unchanged, does the research-only trapped-chain restart (a) cut lotka_volterra trapped chains on 60 fresh seeds with no false positives, (b) leave the 17 house posteriordb models' passes and ESS per gradient intact with every unflagged cell bit-identical and no flag on a cell that passes at the defaults, (c) stay silent on genuine second modes (hmm_drive_0 and a synthetic bimodal target) while the chain-disagreement warning still reports them, and (d) cost under 2 % of wall at its synchronisation point? If all four hold, propose making it the default (which would bump ALGORITHM_REVISION).
baseline_commit: fec52186 (local main: 0.3.0 + WP66 + WP67 merged; the restart flag is default-off)
library: unchanged from WP67 (8887a0f0): WarmupConfig::with_trapped_chain_restart(TrappedChainRestartConfig::step_rule()), research feature; nothing re-tuned

machine.box: AWS EC2 c7a.4xlarge, 16 dedicated AMD cores (no SMT), 32 GB, Ubuntu 24.04, Rust 1.88.0, Python 3.12.3
machine.lane: lane 4, cores 12-15; every build and cell under taskset -c 12-15; RAYON_NUM_THREADS=4, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, TMPDIR under the lane
machine.co_tenancy: other lanes run concurrently on cores 0-11 (shared L3 and memory bandwidth): wall-clock numbers are 'pinned, co-tenanted' and arm (d) is read only as a restart/defaults ratio; gradients, ESS per gradient, hashes and pass counts are unaffected

models_build: prepare_models.py (unchanged from WP67): Stan programs and data from the shared read-only posteriordb checkout, BridgeStan 2.9.0 source tarball (sha256 b6034f83fb2ffb71ce7be9525b7dded1a225e9a4eaf4b75d4c7e97e3ade05a4c) under the lane, gcc 13.3.0, no STAN_THREADS; the 7 WP67 libraries are reused byte-identically and the 10 others are built the same way; hashes in artifacts/models.json

posteriordb.access: read-only shared checkout; reference draws read directly from reference_posteriors/draws/draws/*.json.zip

sampler: owalnuts::sampler: Metric::diagonal() (default), Tuning::default() (RejectLeaf), Limits::admit_worst_case(), 4 chains x 1,000 warmup / 1,000 draws on 4 threads (arm D: chains x 1,000/1,000 on min(chains, 4) threads), starts Init::default() = Init::best_of(16) drawn by candidate_starts exactly as Sampler::run_with_init
detector: unchanged from WP67: flag chain c iff its step at transition 99 (the last transition of the first slow window) is below 0.1 x the median over chains; checked once with the chains synchronised there; skipped with < 3 chains
restart_action: unchanged from WP67: the flagged chain reruns the full schedule from transition 0 from the best of 16 fresh uniform(-2, 2) candidates on an independent seed stream, initial metric and step, fresh dual averaging and RNG stream; at most once per chain

blocks.name: C
blocks.note: genuine second mode: 952202 (WP52 hidden-mode cell, one chain in a second mode for its first 46 retained draws) and 600602 / 600605 (WP60: one best_of_16 chain in a second mode each) are declared targeted replications on a different build (Windows -> Linux), so the second mode need not reappear; 6903101-6903103 are fresh

blocks.name: M
blocks.note: synthetic well-separated bimodal target (the WP52 two-mode target: d = 10, 0.7 N(+4 e1, I) + 0.3 N(-4 e1, I), 8 SD apart), fresh seeds

blocks.name: D
blocks.note: 100-D standard Gaussian; one process per (chain count, repeat); in each, one untimed warm-up run then 7 interleaved (defaults, restart) pairs, order reversed on odd repeats; repeat ratio = median restart wall / median defaults wall

blocks_note: block B's models field means the house_models list (17 models)
cell_order: C, M, D, A, B in that order; within C/M/A seeds in listed order, defaults then restart; D chain counts ascending, repeats ascending; B models in listed order, seeds ascending, defaults then restart. Strictly sequential, one harness process per cell, no cell rerun; failures are results. 12 + 12 + 15 + 120 + 102 = 261 cells.
seeds_verified_unused: git grep -w over the repository at fec52186 and the protocol.json / PREREGISTRATION.md of every sibling worktree find none of 6901001-6901060, 6902001-6902003, 6903101-6903103, 6903201-6903206, 6904001-6904005 or 6909901 (952202, 600602, 600605 are declared targeted replications)

gates.lotka_efficacy_also: max |z| <= 4 on arm A cells only (the WP57/WP67 lotka gate); arms B and C use the v7 gates without z
gates.note: ArviZ 0.23.4 rank R-hat, bulk ESS, tail ESS (0.05/0.95), mean MCSE on every posteriordb reference parameter (v7 code); a cell that errors or times out fails every gate

definitions.chain_shift: per chain, max over reference parameters of |chain mean - reference mean| / reference SD
definitions.trapped_chain: arm A: a chain of a completed cell with shift > 3; in a cell that did not complete, every chain that had not finished
definitions.flagged_chain: restart arm: a chain the library restarted; defaults arm: the detector emulated on the defaults run's transition-99 steps
definitions.false_positive_a: a chain flagged in arm A whose defaults counterpart is not trapped
definitions.false_positive_b: any flagged chain in a block-B cell whose defaults cell passes every gate
definitions.firing: a restart-arm cell with a flagged chain (or a defaults cell whose emulated set is non-empty)
definitions.second_mode_cell_two_mode: a two-mode cell whose chains do not all end in the same mode (mixed end modes)
definitions.warning_reports_it: Summary::chain_warnings (Posterior::chain_warnings) is non-empty on the cell
definitions.efficiency: per cell min bulk ESS / total target calls (start search, abandoned runs, replacement pools included); per model geometric mean over seeds where both arms completed; ratio restart / defaults; geometric mean over the 17 models
definitions.sync_overhead: per chain count, the median over the 5 repeats of the repeat ratio (median restart wall / median defaults wall), minus 1
definitions.fingerprint: on every defaults/restart pair of arms A, B, C: flagged sets equal and transition-99 steps equal; a non-firing pair bit-identical (all-chain draw hash and total target calls); every unflagged chain of a firing pair bit-identical (draw hash and target calls); arm D: every run of a cell has the same draw hash and target calls

predictions.P1: arm A: defaults has 4-16 trapped chains of 240 (WP57 + WP67 saw 4 of 192 at the defaults on these code paths, about 2 %, but with targeted seeds included); restart has at most 1
predictions.P2: arm A: the detector flags every defaults trapped chain that reached transition 99 (sensitivity 1) and no other chain (0 false positives)
predictions.P3: arm B: the detector fires only on lotka_volterra cells; 0 flags on cells that pass at the defaults; passes restart >= defaults; geomean ESS/gradient ratio >= 1.00 (1.0000 on every model the rule never fires on)
predictions.P4: arm C: 0 firings on all 24 cells (a mode is not a trap: the mode's step is not 10x smaller); on every hmm_drive_0 cell with a second-mode chain and on every mixed-mode two-mode cell the chain-disagreement warning is non-empty
predictions.P4_expectation: my own expectation, recorded separately: the warning is reliable for a single minority chain but WP52 showed it silent on 2 of 3 mixed two-mode cells (two chains per mode, leave-one-out R-hat cannot isolate a chain), so I expect P4's warning half to fail on 2-2 splits, while max split R-hat > 1.01 reports every mixed cell
predictions.P5: arm D: sync overhead < 2 % at 4 and 16 chains; at 1 chain the restart path is not entered (fewer than 3 chains) so the ratio measures only timing noise
predictions.P6: fingerprint holds on every pair and every arm-D cell

decision_rule.a: arm A: restart trapped chains < defaults trapped chains (so defaults needs >= 1) and 0 false positives (false_positive_a)
decision_rule.b: arm B: passes restart >= defaults of 51, geomean ESS/gradient ratio >= 0.99, every unflagged cell bit-identical (fingerprint), and 0 false_positive_b
decision_rule.c: arm C: zero firings over all 24 cells (both arms, actual and emulated)
decision_rule.d: arm D: sync overhead < 0.02 at 4 chains and at 16 chains
decision_rule.fingerprint_any_arm: a fingerprint failure anywhere is an implementation fault: verdict FAILED (implementation)
decision_rule.verdict: PROPOSE THE DEFAULT iff a, b, c and d all hold and the fingerprint holds; a default change would bump ALGORITHM_REVISION and needs the house v7-style validation afterwards. Otherwise DO NOT PROPOSE. The prediction about the chain-disagreement warning (P4, second half) is reported but is not a decision clause.
